policy: Every occurrence is checked against the complete immutable KJV verse. Confirmed active records were separately approved; proposals remain inactive.

records.reason: Champaign names the open, level country where the Canaanites dwell; it is not the modern place name Champagne.
records.sourceText: Are they not on the other side Jordan, by the way where the sun goeth down, in the land of the Canaanites, which dwell in the champaign over against Gilgal, beside the plains of Moreh?

records.reason: Minish means diminish. The officers are forbidden to reduce any part of the daily brick requirement.
records.sourceText: And the officers of the children of Israel did see that they were in evil case, after it was said, Ye shall not minish ought from your bricks of your daily task.

records.reason: Assay is the obsolete verb try or attempt, and commune here is the act of speaking with Job.
records.sourceText: If we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking?

records.reason: Neesings is an obsolete form referring to the creature’s sneezes, not a separate physical feature.
records.activeReason: Context-safe standalone occurrence allowed by the conservative v1 whitelist.
records.sourceText: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

records.reason: Trow is the archaic verb think or believe. The phrase closes the rhetorical question without changing its force.
records.sourceText: Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him I trow not

records.reason: Eschew is an archaic command to avoid or turn away from evil; the following command to do good remains intact.
records.sourceText: Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.

records.expected: the noise of the bruit is come
records.proposedReplacement: the sound of the news is coming
records.reason: Bruit here is an approaching report heard as a sound from the north, not the modern medical term.
records.sourceText: Behold, the noise of the bruit is come, and a great commotion out of the north country, to make the cities of Judah desolate, and a den of dragons.

records.reason: Bruit here is the report or news of Nineveh’s fall that causes the hearers to clap, not a physical murmur.
records.sourceText: There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?

records.reason: Leasing is the obsolete noun falsehood. It parallels vanity and does not refer to renting property.
records.sourceText: O ye sons of men, how long will ye turn my glory into shame? how long will ye love vanity, and seek after leasing? Selah.

records.reason: Leasing is the obsolete noun falsehood; the next clause’s deceitful man confirms the lying context.
records.sourceText: Thou shalt destroy them that speak leasing: the LORD will abhor the bloody and deceitful man.

records.reason: Anon has its archaic immediate sense: the hearer receives the word at once with joy.
records.sourceText: But he that received the seed into stony places the same is he that heareth the word and anon with joy receiveth it

records.reason: Anon has its archaic immediate sense: those present tell Jesus about the sick woman without delay.
records.sourceText: But Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever, and anon they tell him of her.

records.reason: Ensample is the archaic form of example; the destroyed cities serve as a warning to later ungodly people.
records.sourceText: And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;

records.reason: Ensample is the archaic form of example; Paul describes conduct the readers can follow.
records.sourceText: Not because we have not power, but to make ourselves an ensample unto you to follow us.

records.reason: Ensample is the archaic form of example; Paul asks readers to observe people who follow the apostolic pattern.
records.sourceText: Brethren, be followers together of me, and mark them which walk so as ye have us for an ensample.

records.reason: Wot is the archaic present-tense verb know. Peter states that the people and rulers acted through ignorance.
records.sourceText: And now, brethren, I wot that through ignorance ye did it, as did also your rulers.

records.reason: Wot is the archaic verb know. The speakers claim that they do not know what happened to Moses.
records.sourceText: Saying unto Aaron, Make us gods to go before us: for as for this Moses, which brought us out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.

records.reason: Wot is the archaic verb know. The people claim that they do not know what happened to Moses.
records.sourceText: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.

records.reason: Wot is the archaic verb know. Aaron repeats the people’s claim that they do not know what happened to Moses.
records.sourceText: For they said unto me, Make us gods, which shall go before us: for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.

records.reason: Wot is the archaic verb know. Abimelech denies knowing who dug the well.
records.sourceText: And Abimelech said, I wot not who hath done this thing: neither didst thou tell me, neither yet heard I of it, but to day.

records.reason: The complete question was reviewed against close English controls; do you not know preserves the question while modernizing wot and its word order.
records.activeReason: Wot is an obsolete form of know. The Hebrew question, the close NKJV comparison, and the American ASV control all preserve a direct question without changing Joseph’s claim about divination.
records.sourceText: And Joseph said unto them, What deed is this that ye have done? wot ye not that such a man as I can certainly divine?

records.reason: Wot is the archaic verb know. Rahab says that she does not know where the men went.
records.sourceText: And it came to pass about the time of shutting of the gate, when it was dark, that the men went out: whither the men went I wot not: pursue after them quickly; for ye shall overtake them.

records.reason: Wot is the archaic verb know. Balak states what he believes about Balaam’s blessing and curse.
records.sourceText: Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me: peradventure I shall prevail, that we may smite them, and that I may drive them out of the land: for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.

records.reason: Wot is the archaic verb know. Paul says that he does not know which outcome to choose.
records.sourceText: But if I live in the flesh, this is the fruit of my labour: yet what I shall choose I wot not.

records.reason: The complete question was reviewed against close English controls; do you not know preserves the question while modernizing wot and its word order.
records.activeReason: Wot is an obsolete form of know. The Greek question and the close NKJV and American ASV controls preserve the same appeal to what Scripture says.
records.sourceText: God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel, saying,

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. Peter does not know that the angelic rescue is real.
records.sourceText: And he went out, and followed him; and wist not that it was true which was done by the angel; but thought he saw a vision.

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. Paul says that he did not know the speaker was the high priest.
records.sourceText: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. The Israelites do not recognize the manna.
records.sourceText: And when the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which the LORD hath given you to eat.

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. Moses is unaware that his face is shining.
records.sourceText: ¶ And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him.

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. Samson is unaware that the LORD has departed from him.
records.sourceText: And she said, The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times before, and shake myself. And he wist not that the LORD was departed from him.

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. The healed man does not know Jesus’ identity.
records.sourceText: And he that was healed wist not who it was: for Jesus had conveyed himself away, a multitude being in that place.

records.expected: I wist not whence they were
records.proposedReplacement: I did not know where they came from
records.reason: Wist means knew and whence means from where. The complete phrase preserves Rahab’s claim while avoiding an incomplete word-by-word modernization.
records.sourceText: And the woman took the two men, and hid them, and said thus, There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were:

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. The king of Ai is unaware of the ambush behind the city.
records.sourceText: ¶ And it came to pass, when the king of Ai saw it, that they hasted and rose up early, and the men of the city went out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at a time appointed, before the plain; but he wist not that there were liers in ambush against him behind the city.

records.proposedReplacement: though he did not know it
records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. The clause concerns an unknowingly committed offense.
records.sourceText: ¶ And if a soul sin, and commit any of these things which are forbidden to be done by the commandments of the LORD; though he wist it not, yet is he guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. The clause describes the person’s ignorance of the error.
records.sourceText: And he shall bring a ram without blemish out of the flock, with thy estimation, for a trespass offering, unto the priest: and the priest shall make an atonement for him concerning his ignorance wherein he erred and wist it not, and it shall be forgiven him.

records.reason: The two-question structure was reviewed in Greek and close English controls; the replacement restores the question boundary and modernizes wist without changing the statement that follows.
records.activeReason: Wist is the obsolete past tense of know. The Greek contains two questions, and the close English comparisons confirm the question boundary missing from the normalized source display.
records.sourceText: And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. Peter does not know what to say because of fear.
records.sourceText: For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.

records.reason: Wist is the archaic past-tense verb knew. The disciples do not know what answer to give Jesus.
records.sourceText: And when he returned, he found them asleep again, (for their eyes were heavy,) neither wist they what to answer him.
